aria: Animated recap of the Trail Blazers' 116 to 111 home win over San Antonio: Deni Avdija's bank-shot 3-pointer with 38 seconds left that made it 114 to 109, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Avdija's 33 points, 12 rebounds and 7 assists, the top scorers, how the Blazers won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Trail Blazers' 116–111 home win over San Antonio on Nov 25, 2026: all 116 Portland points and all 111 San Antonio points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (37 of 94, 19 of 50 from three, 23 of 31 FT for Portland; 39 of 90, 10 of 36, 23 of 29 for San Antonio), rebounds (50–55), assists (29–21) and steals (8–5). StatMuse also has points off turnovers (14–9), fast-break points (13–5) and second-chance points (11–18). The quarter scores (38–22–24–32 to 35–22–30–24) match StatMuse, the FOX Sports play-by-play and VAVEL; 60–57 Portland at the half is also in Fast Break Journal and Roundtable Sports, and 87–84 San Antonio after three follows from Devin Vassell's fadeaway three at the third-quarter buzzer (StatMuse; FOX Sports). Biggest leads (Portland 7, San Antonio 3) are on StatMuse. Records are from the game stories (Blazers 12–6, Spurs 15–4; StatMuse; Fast Break Journal; Blazers On SI); ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

It was the Spurs' first road loss of the season after an 8–0 start away from home (Yahoo Sports; Fast Break Journal; The Ticket). Victor Wembanyama had 44 points and 16 rebounds (StatMuse); his alley-oop dunk from Stephon Castle tied it 109–109 with 2:00 left (StatMuse; FOX Sports; The Ticket). Portland played without Ja Morant, Vit Krejci, Shaedon Sharpe and Chris Youngblood; San Antonio without De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, Tobias Harris and Jayden Quaintance (Fast Break Journal). Portland, San Antonio, Golden State and the Lakers are all 2–1 in NBA Cup group play with one game left on Friday (Fast Break Journal; The Ticket; SB Nation). Next: Portland hosts Golden State on Friday (Fast Break Journal; FOX Sports schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Deni Avdija's bank-shot 3-pointer with 38 seconds left that made it 114–109: StatMuse has "D. Avdija makes 26' bank three Assisted by D. Lillard" at 0:38 of the fourth for 111–109 to 114–109, and the FOX Sports play-by-play has "Deni Avdija makes three point bank jump shot (Damian Lillard assists)". The Ticket: Lillard drove, saw Wembanyama waiting as the shot clock wound down, and fired the pass back to Avdija, who banked in a 3-pointer for a five-point lead. So the board's Blazers +2 to +5 is 111–109 to 114–109. Written stories time it at 37.9 or 38.6 seconds; the play-by-play has 0:38, which is what the clock shows. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Portland Trail Blazers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Avdija's listed 6-foot-8 and 228 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), with arms at the default length because neither reports a wingspan, in the Trail Blazers' home kit with No. 8 (Wikipedia; FOX Sports) and a lighter skin tone; he has no approved look yet (proposed in kit/looks.json). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
